time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If squinting or blinking does not improve
If the eye remains partly or fully closed
If redness, swelling, or discharge continues or worsens
If the eye becomes cloudy or looks different from the other eye
If your dog seems sensitive to light or shows signs of vision changes
If a lump on the eyelid grows, changes, or begins to irritate the eye

home_care_tips.title: Eye – Home Care Tips
contents: Avoid getting shampoo or grooming products in your pet’s eyes
Gently wipe away any discharge with warm water and soft gauze when needed
Keep hair around the eyes neatly groomed so it does not touch the surface
Consider adding a daily eye-support supplement containing omega-3s and antioxidants to help maintain healthy vision and tear balance

details.title: What It Is
contents: Excessive tearing that keeps the eye area wet and can turn the surrounding fur brown or reddish.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Gently wipe away tears with sterile saline and soft gauze
Have a groomer keep hair from touching the eyes
If new treats were introduced recently, pause them for 1–2 weeks

details.title: What It Is
contents: A condition where the lower eyelid droops outward, leaving part of the eye more exposed.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Keep the eyelids clean if discharge develops
Avoid dusty or windy environments when possible

details.title: What It Is
contents: A condition where the third eyelid (normally hidden) protrudes and appears as a red, swollen lump.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone if rubbing continues

details.title: What It Is
contents: The white part of the eye appears redder than usual, with more visible blood vessels.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Let your dog rest in a calm, dim space
Avoid smoke, sprays, or strong scents
Limit stressful changes in the home

details.title: What It Is
contents: A cloudy or hazy appearance on the surface of the eye.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Watch for signs of reduced vision

details.title: What It Is
contents: Discharge that collects around the eye and may appear clear, white, yellow, or brown.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Gently wipe with sterile saline and soft gauze
Monitor for color or amount changes

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling of the white part of the eye or the pink inner tissue.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone if rubbing continues
Limit exposure to dust and wind

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling and thickening of the eyelids.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Avoid touching or squeezing the eyelids

details.title: What It Is
contents: A lump or bump on the eyelid area.

details.title: Possible Causes
contents: Less commonly, a more serious tumor

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Do not squeeze or manipulate the lump
Monitor for changes in size or shape

time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If redness or irritation is spreading or getting worse
If your dog continues scratching frequently despite basic care
If you notice open sores, bleeding, or moist irritated patches
If the skin develops a persistent strong or unusual odor
If a lump grows, changes in appearance, or becomes red or painful

home_care_tips.title: Skin – Home Care Tips
contents: After bathing, gently dry areas with limited airflow—such as the armpits, groin, and between the toes—using a soft towel or a low, cool dryer setting
Frequent paw licking may be related to skin irritation, boredom, or stress. Providing regular exercise and enrichment may help reduce licking
Keep a record of shampoos, grooming products, foods, and treats. Changes in products or ingredients may sometimes contribute to skin irritation
A daily skin-support supplement containing omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids may help maintain normal skin and coat health

details.title: What It Is
contents: An area of skin that appears redder than your dog’s normal skin color.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Avoid recent irritants such as grass, new shampoos, detergents, or cleaners
Pause newly introduced treats or supplements for 1–2 weeks
Use a cone if licking continues

details.title: What It Is
contents: A darkened area of skin that may be naturally darker, or has gradually become darker due to long-standing inflammation or irritation.

details.title: Possible Causes
contents: Normal skin variation in some dogs

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Reduce friction from harnesses or collars
Continue previously prescribed allergy management if applicable
Limit excessive sun exposure on lightly haired areas

details.title: What It Is
contents: Thickened and roughened skin caused by chronic inflammation or repeated itching or irritation.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone if licking or scratching continues
Keep the area clean and well dried

details.title: What It Is
contents: A condition where the skin surface is peeled away, or deeper damage creates a sunken area.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone to prevent licking

details.title: What It Is
contents: Pustule: Small bumps filled with pus
Crust: Hardened, dried discharge or skin fluids on the surface
When affecting the ear, crusts may be dried discharge from inside the ear that has hardened on the outer ear.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Do not squeeze or pick at lesions
Use a cone if licking continues
Pause newly introduced treats for 1–2 weeks
If previously recommended by your veterinarian, use a dog-specific antiseptic wash

details.title: What It Is
contents: A rounded lump visible on or under the skin.

details.title: Possible Causes
contents: Less commonly, a more serious tumor

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Do not squeeze or manipulate the lump
Take a photo weekly to monitor size
Measure with a ruler for comparison

details.title: What It Is
contents: White or yellow flakes or scales that rise from or adhere to the skin.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Brush regularly to remove loose flakes
Use a mild, dog-specific moisturizing shampoo

time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If your dog won’t stop shaking their head or scratching despite basic care
If redness or swelling inside the ear is increasing
If thick discharge or heavy buildup continues despite gentle cleaning
If your dog seems painful when the ear is touched
If head tilting or balance issues continue
If a lump grows, changes in appearance, or becomes red or painful

home_care_tips.title: Ear – Home Care Tips
contents: Keep ears clean and dry, especially after bathing or swimming
Use ear cleanser only as directed and stop if redness or increased irritation develops
Track any changes in food or treats, as food allergies may affect ear health
A daily skin- and ear-support supplement containing omega-3 fatty acids may help maintain normal ear health

time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If your dog shows signs of mouth pain when eating or chewing
If gums are red, swollen, or bleeding
If bad breath becomes noticeably worse
If you notice loose teeth or heavy tartar buildup
If there’s no improvement despite basic dental care

home_care_tips.title: Teeth - Home Care Tips
contents: Brush your dog’s teeth daily, or at least 2–3 times per week, using pet-safe toothpaste and a soft toothbrush
If brushing is difficult, dental chews or dental diets may help manage plaque

details.title: What It Is
contents: Hardened dental plaque on the tooth surface that becomes a yellow, brown, or gray, rock-like deposit.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Brush your dog’s teeth daily using dog-specific toothpaste
Offer dental chews designed to reduce plaque
Provide safe chew toys to help control buildup

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling, redness, or bleeding of the gums.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Start gentle daily brushing if tolerated
Use dental wipes if brushing is difficult
Avoid hard bones or objects that may irritate the gums
Consider a dental rinse made for dogs

time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If squinting continues or the eye remains partly or fully closed
If redness, swelling, or discharge does not improve or worsens
If the eye becomes cloudy, develops a dark spot, or looks different from the other eye
If your cat seems sensitive to light or shows signs of eye pain
If your cat becomes less active, hides more than usual, or eats less

home_care_tips.title: Eye – Home Care Tips
contents: Use a soft gauze pad moistened with warm water to gently clean eye discharge
Keep your cat away from scented candles, sprays, and strong household fragrances that may irritate the eyes
If your cat has a history of feline herpesvirus, try to reduce stress and maintain a consistent environment, as stress may trigger flare-ups
A daily eye-support supplement containing omega-3s and antioxidants may help maintain normal immune and eye health

details.title: What It Is
contents: Discharge that collects around the eye and may appear clear, white, yellow, or brown.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Gently clean discharge with sterile saline and soft gauze
Check for sneezing, nasal discharge, or reduced appetite

details.title: What It Is
contents: A brown or black spot on the eye surface (cornea) that may indicate damaged tissue.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone if rubbing continues

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling and thickening of the eyelids.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Avoid touching or squeezing the eyelids
Use a cone if rubbing continues

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling of the white part of the eye or the pink inner tissue.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Use a cone if rubbing continues
If irritation persists, temporarily remove new litter, sprays, or cleaners

details.title: What It Is
contents: The white part of the eye appears redder than usual, with more visible blood vessels.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Let your cat rest in a quiet, dim space
Limit stressful changes in the home

time_to_see_a_vet.title: Time to see a vet
contents: If your cat eats less or seems hesitant to eat
If your cat avoids chewing or drops food while eating
If gums are red, swollen, or bleeding
If you notice drooling or pawing at the mouth
If bad breath becomes noticeably worse

home_care_tips.title: Teeth – Home Care Tips
contents: Brush your cat’s teeth daily, or at least a few times per week, using pet-safe toothpaste and a soft-bristled toothbrush
If brushing is difficult, dental treats or dental diets may help manage plaque

details.title: What It Is
contents: Hardened dental plaque on the tooth surface that becomes a yellow, brown, or gray, rock-like deposit.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Start brushing slowly if your cat tolerates it
Try dental wipes if brushing is difficult
Offer dental treats made for tartar control

details.title: What It Is
contents: Swelling, redness, or bleeding of the gums.

details.title: What You Can Do
contents: Avoid hard treats or dry food that may irritate the gums
Offer softer food if chewing seems uncomfortable
Keep the mouth area clean if drooling occurs
